feature.title: RAM prefetch: promote landed rows into the tier map before the target layer

brief.goal: A speculative row that has landed in the prefetch pool before its target layer's record is published becomes an ordinary RAM-tier entry in that layer's map, so the GPU types it as a RAM hit (eligible for the CPU/link split) instead of a miss. Opt-in behind a flag, default off; the device code is unchanged.
criteria: With `SGLANG_DSV41_RAM_PREFETCH_PROMOTE=1`, a landed pool row of row r is mapped (expert -> its pool slot) in row r's map delta that the device applies at row r's next post, and that post types the expert as a hit (HIT_COPY, HIT_SM or HIT_CPU), not MISS_GPU or MISS_CPU.

A promoted row is never read from NVMe again for that record, whatever lane kind the device would have given it as a miss (closes the bypass at `ram_tier.h:2711`, where an unforced miss ignores the pool).

Every row's delta for chain N is published before the host serves row r's record of chain N+1; no post waits on an unpublished delta past today's deadline, and no chain check (`ram_tier.h:2144`, `:2737`) fails, over a full served DSpark capture.
A delta never exceeds `Wire::kDeltaMaxEntries`; promotions that do not fit are skipped and counted.
With the flag off, publication timing and delta bytes are identical to today (same tests green, unchanged order).

Every counter in Design §5 appears in the RAM-miss thread counters line and in `spec_margin_capture.py`'s `counters.json`, is zero with the flag off, and has a unit test that drives it to a known nonzero value.
The InstrBuild trace emits one `delta_publish` event per deferred delta (row, chain, trigger, promoted count), so a capture can measure the time from a delta's write to its row's next record.
The served A/B report states, per assumption in Design §5, the counter values and whether the assumption held.
Served outputs with the flag on are identical to flag off over the capture's sessions (same text per session).

items.title: Design
items.summary: - Today: a miss record of row r (chain N) is served; each reporting group reports its part; the last reporter writes the delta (tag N) in reserve_victims_locked before any read (ram_tier.h:2735), then release_swapped. - With the flag: the last reporter combines as today but stores the combined delt…
items.body:
### 1. Deferred publication
- Today: a miss record of row r (chain N) is served; each reporting group reports its part; the last reporter writes
  the delta (tag N) in `reserve_victims_locked` before any read (`ram_tier.h:2735`), then `release_swapped`.
- With the flag: the last reporter combines as today but stores the combined delta as row r's *pending delta*
  (entries, staging lists, chain N) in `NumaNodeDistributor` instead of writing it, unless row r is publish-immediate
  (Decisions). Swaps done by row r's own record keep `freed_at = N` and are released when the pending delta is written.
- Row r's pending delta is written by the service thread that serves row r-1's next record (any chain, miss or not,
  any group: whichever group's `handle_record` for row r-1 first claims the pending delta, by CAS on a per-row
  pending word). It is written before that thread serves row r-1's lanes, so it is visible before row r-1's gate can
  open and therefore before row r's post.
- Backstop: a record of row r itself, or a record of any row after r in the forward order arriving while row r's delta
  is pending, writes it first. So a skipped or reordered row r-1 never strands it; the deferral never delays past the
  point today's protocol would need it.

- Known cost: when row r-1's record has no host lane, the device may not wait on the host for it, so row r's post can
  reach `await_map_delta` before the host has served row r-1 and spin for that service latency (the polling thread's
  pickup, tens of us). The served capture measures it (per-row gap before rows with a deferred delta); if it shows,
  the trigger moves earlier (the moment row r's last pool read resolves).

### 2. Promotion at publish
- The claiming thread, before writing row r's pending delta, for each group g (taking g's pool mutex, then row r's
  tier lock in the existing order): for each pool entry of (r, g) in kPoolLanded, picks a victim with
  `take_victim_locked(group, r, {}, &old)`, appends {old, -1} and {expert, pool slot} to the pending entries if two
  slots fit under `kDeltaMaxEntries`, maps the expert in the tier and host mirror as `commit_inserted_locked` does,
  marks the victim kSpec and the entry kPoolSwapped with `slot = victim`, `freed_at = N`; counts
  `spec_promoted_early`, or `spec_promote_skipped` when it does not fit or has no victim.
- Cross-group access is through each group's own tier and pool mutex; the claimer does not touch another group's
  service state beyond those locked structures.
- Entries in kPoolReading are left; a later forced miss still promotes or swaps them as today.

### 3. Device view
- Unchanged: row r's post awaits tag N, applies the delta (now including promotions), types lanes from the map. A
  promoted expert is mapped, so it is a hit and joins the split's eligible lanes; the GPU never needed to know it was
  prefetched.
- The cross-row apply kernel (`lease_kernels.cuh:327`) skips a row whose tag is not yet written, so deferral is safe
  there.

### 5. Assumptions and the counters that test them
Each sprint choice rests on an assumption; each has a counter (RAM-miss thread counters, per group summed like the
existing ones) so a capture shows when it fails. Names are final; all are zero with the flag off.

| Assumption | Counter(s) | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| Most landed rows ride a pending delta (rows whose last record had a miss) | `spec_promoted_early` (promoted), `spec_promote_no_delta` (landed, row had no pending delta) | `no_delta` is a large share of landed-at-publish rows: the device-chain limit matters, and covering miss-free rows (device change) is worth it |
| Leftover delta room is enough | `spec_promote_no_room` | nonzero share of promotions: raise `kDeltaMaxEntries` (layout change) |
| A victim is always available | `spec_promote_no_victim` | nonzero |
| Blind LRU victims rarely hit the layer's routes | `spec_promote_victim_routed` (at row r's next record, a miss lane whose expert a promotion of this chain evicted) | comparable to `spec_promoted_early` x hit rate: victims need the routes, so promote later or protect recent hits |
| Promoted rows are used | `spec_promote_used` (at row r's next record, a hit lane on an expert promoted for this chain) | low against `spec_promoted_early`: promotions displace useful rows for little gain |
| Most rows have landed by publish time | `spec_promote_reading` (a pool entry of row r still reading at publish; left to the demand-time swap) | large: the trigger is too early; move it later or wait |
| The deferral never makes a post wait | `spec_publish_backstop` (a pending delta written by the backstop, not by row r-1's serve), plus the `delta_publish` event's time against row r's next record | backstop nonzero, or delta write within a few us of row r's record: move the trigger earlier |
| Bypassed unforced misses shrink | existing `rows_read` against forced CPU misses minus pool-served (the 2026-10-13 `read_split.py` measure) | "other reads" do not fall with the flag on |

### 6. Failure handling
- A pending delta still unwritten at shutdown or quiesce is written by the quiescer before it returns.
- Any violation (chain mismatch, two claimers) fail-stops through `fail_record`, as today's chain checks do.

# RAM prefetch: promote landed rows into the tier map before the target layer

## Goal
A speculative row that has landed in the prefetch pool before its target layer's record is published becomes an
ordinary RAM-tier entry in that layer's map, so the GPU types it as a RAM hit (eligible for the CPU/link split) instead
of a miss. Opt-in behind a flag, default off; the device code is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- With `SGLANG_DSV41_RAM_PREFETCH_PROMOTE=1`, a landed pool row of row r is mapped (expert -> its pool slot) in row r's
  map delta that the device applies at row r's next post, and that post types the expert as a hit (HIT_COPY, HIT_SM or
  HIT_CPU), not MISS_GPU or MISS_CPU.
- A promoted row is never read from NVMe again for that record, whatever lane kind the device would have given it as
  a miss (closes the bypass at `ram_tier.h:2711`, where an unforced miss ignores the pool).
- Every row's delta for chain N is published before the host serves row r's record of chain N+1; no post waits on an
  unpublished delta past today's deadline, and no chain check (`ram_tier.h:2144`, `:2737`) fails, over a full served
  DSpark capture.
- A delta never exceeds `Wire::kDeltaMaxEntries`; promotions that do not fit are skipped and counted.
- With the flag off, publication timing and delta bytes are identical to today (same tests green, unchanged order).
- Every counter in Design §5 appears in the RAM-miss thread counters line and in `spec_margin_capture.py`'s
  `counters.json`, is zero with the flag off, and has a unit test that drives it to a known nonzero value.
- The InstrBuild trace emits one `delta_publish` event per deferred delta (row, chain, trigger, promoted count), so a
  capture can measure the time from a delta's write to its row's next record.
- The served A/B report states, per assumption in Design §5, the counter values and whether the assumption held.
- Served outputs with the flag on are identical to flag off over the capture's sessions (same text per session).

## Decisions
- Approach: defer each row's map delta from the end of its own record to the serving of the previous row's record in
  the next forward, and fold that row's landed pool rows into it (owner's idea, 2026-10-13). Rejected: copying a
  pooled row into the miss's staging slot at demand time (host memcpy per miss, covers only misses, keeps the bypass
  structure) and a device-visible pool state (device change).
- Promotion only rides a delta that is already pending: the device advances a row's chain only on a record with a
  miss (`lease_kernels.cuh:274`), so a row whose last record had no miss has no delta to carry a promotion in v1. The
  existing demand-time swap (`take_pooled_locked`) stays for those rows and for rows still reading at publish time.
- Victims for promotions are chosen by `take_victim_locked` with no wanted list (the target layer's routes are not
  known yet); this can evict an expert the layer then routes to, which becomes an ordinary miss.
- Rows that no source row targets (`RamPrefetchConfig::target` maps nothing to them) and row 0 publish immediately, as
  today: nothing can be promoted into them.
- Flag `SGLANG_DSV41_RAM_PREFETCH_PROMOTE` (EnvBool False), requires the RAM prefetch; launch refuses it otherwise.
- Sprint speed (owner, 2026-10-13): one feature, no device change, no layout change.

## Rules
- No change to device code, `lease_layout.h`, the delta wire format or `Wire::kDeltaMaxEntries`.
- Follow the existing threading contract in `host/ram_prefetch.h`: pool entry transitions out of landed only under
  the group's pool mutex; a promoted entry becomes kPoolSwapped holding its victim until the delta that evicts the
  victim is published, then `release_swapped` empties it (same lifecycle as a demand-time swap).
- The publisher is still exactly one thread per (row, chain), chosen by `NumaNodeDistributor`'s report combine.
- Env var per `.claude/skills/env-var-conventions`; add the `Dsv41Config` field and its default test, the env docs
  row, and the `DSV41_REFERENCE.md` §32 row.
- Update `analysis/dsv41-drive/LEASE_PROTOCOL.md` with the deferred-publication rule.
- Run protocol: tests on divix01 via the checks runner; served captures only in private worktrees; production untouched.

## Non-goals
- No device-side promotion for rows whose last record had no miss (would need the host to advance the chain).
- No change to scoring, thresholds, cap, horizon or the idle-drive reader.
- No default flip; the owner decides after the A/B.
- No change to how forced misses that find a pool row still reading are served (they keep waiting, as today).

## Open questions

## Design

### 1. Deferred publication
- Today: a miss record of row r (chain N) is served; each reporting group reports its part; the last reporter writes
  the delta (tag N) in `reserve_victims_locked` before any read (`ram_tier.h:2735`), then `release_swapped`.
- With the flag: the last reporter combines as today but stores the combined delta as row r's *pending delta*
  (entries, staging lists, chain N) in `NumaNodeDistributor` instead of writing it, unless row r is publish-immediate
  (Decisions). Swaps done by row r's own record keep `freed_at = N` and are released when the pending delta is written.
- Row r's pending delta is written by the service thread that serves row r-1's next record (any chain, miss or not,
  any group: whichever group's `handle_record` for row r-1 first claims the pending delta, by CAS on a per-row
  pending word). It is written before that thread serves row r-1's lanes, so it is visible before row r-1's gate can
  open and therefore before row r's post.
- Backstop: a record of row r itself, or a record of any row after r in the forward order arriving while row r's delta
  is pending, writes it first. So a skipped or reordered row r-1 never strands it; the deferral never delays past the
  point today's protocol would need it.

- Known cost: when row r-1's record has no host lane, the device may not wait on the host for it, so row r's post can
  reach `await_map_delta` before the host has served row r-1 and spin for that service latency (the polling thread's
  pickup, tens of us). The served capture measures it (per-row gap before rows with a deferred delta); if it shows,
  the trigger moves earlier (the moment row r's last pool read resolves).

### 2. Promotion at publish
- The claiming thread, before writing row r's pending delta, for each group g (taking g's pool mutex, then row r's
  tier lock in the existing order): for each pool entry of (r, g) in kPoolLanded, picks a victim with
  `take_victim_locked(group, r, {}, &old)`, appends {old, -1} and {expert, pool slot} to the pending entries if two
  slots fit under `kDeltaMaxEntries`, maps the expert in the tier and host mirror as `commit_inserted_locked` does,
  marks the victim kSpec and the entry kPoolSwapped with `slot = victim`, `freed_at = N`; counts
  `spec_promoted_early`, or `spec_promote_skipped` when it does not fit or has no victim.
- Cross-group access is through each group's own tier and pool mutex; the claimer does not touch another group's
  service state beyond those locked structures.
- Entries in kPoolReading are left; a later forced miss still promotes or swaps them as today.

### 3. Device view
- Unchanged: row r's post awaits tag N, applies the delta (now including promotions), types lanes from the map. A
  promoted expert is mapped, so it is a hit and joins the split's eligible lanes; the GPU never needed to know it was
  prefetched.
- The cross-row apply kernel (`lease_kernels.cuh:327`) skips a row whose tag is not yet written, so deferral is safe
  there.

### 5. Assumptions and the counters that test them
Each sprint choice rests on an assumption; each has a counter (RAM-miss thread counters, per group summed like the
existing ones) so a capture shows when it fails. Names are final; all are zero with the flag off.

| Assumption | Counter(s) | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| Most landed rows ride a pending delta (rows whose last record had a miss) | `spec_promoted_early` (promoted), `spec_promote_no_delta` (landed, row had no pending delta) | `no_delta` is a large share of landed-at-publish rows: the device-chain limit matters, and covering miss-free rows (device change) is worth it |
| Leftover delta room is enough | `spec_promote_no_room` | nonzero share of promotions: raise `kDeltaMaxEntries` (layout change) |
| A victim is always available | `spec_promote_no_victim` | nonzero |
| Blind LRU victims rarely hit the layer's routes | `spec_promote_victim_routed` (at row r's next record, a miss lane whose expert a promotion of this chain evicted) | comparable to `spec_promoted_early` x hit rate: victims need the routes, so promote later or protect recent hits |
| Promoted rows are used | `spec_promote_used` (at row r's next record, a hit lane on an expert promoted for this chain) | low against `spec_promoted_early`: promotions displace useful rows for little gain |
| Most rows have landed by publish time | `spec_promote_reading` (a pool entry of row r still reading at publish; left to the demand-time swap) | large: the trigger is too early; move it later or wait |
| The deferral never makes a post wait | `spec_publish_backstop` (a pending delta written by the backstop, not by row r-1's serve), plus the `delta_publish` event's time against row r's next record | backstop nonzero, or delta write within a few us of row r's record: move the trigger earlier |
| Bypassed unforced misses shrink | existing `rows_read` against forced CPU misses minus pool-served (the 2026-10-13 `read_split.py` measure) | "other reads" do not fall with the flag on |

### 6. Failure handling
- A pending delta still unwritten at shutdown or quiesce is written by the quiescer before it returns.
- Any violation (chain mismatch, two claimers) fail-stops through `fail_record`, as today's chain checks do.

## Testing
- Unit (registered, CPU, through the existing RAM-miss service harness and `tier_sim.py`): flag off, delta bytes and
  publication order unchanged; flag on, a landed pool row of row r appears in row r's delta written while row r-1 is
  served and the device-side map apply types it as a hit; a row with no pending delta is not promoted and counted
  skipped; a full delta skips promotions and counts them; the backstop writes a pending delta when row r-1 is skipped;
  shutdown flushes a pending delta; a promoted entry is released (empty) once its delta is written.
- GPU (`test/manual/dsv41`, `--gpu`): a captured post after a deferred, promoted delta types the promoted expert as a
  hit and reads no NVMe row for it.
- Served: one instrumented capture pair (T3 cap 2, flag off then on, fixed split per
  `RAM_PREFETCH_FIXED_SPLIT_NEXT_HANDOFF.md`), reporting `spec_promoted_early`, demand `rows_read`, outputs per
  session, and the per-layer gate waits; no chain or deadline failures in `server.log`. The report includes the §5
  table filled with the capture's values and a verdict per assumption, recorded in `DSV41_REFERENCE.md` as a new §33
  subsection that also lists the sprint choices (Decisions) and which ones the data says to revisit.

tasks.title: Pending-delta state in NumaNodeDistributor
tasks.intent:
Give each row a single pending delta, claimed by CAS, that holds the combined entries, staging and chain until exactly one thread writes it (S§1.1, R3).
**Steps:**
- Add per-row state beside or in `RowCombine`:
  - `std::atomic<uint64_t> pending` (0 = none, else the chain plus a claimed bit);
  - an entries buffer of `kDeltaMaxEntries` pairs, its count and chain;
  - the stash's forward id;
  - per-row `deferred` flags.
- `set_deferred(std::vector<uint8_t>)` and `deferred(row)`: the owner calls set_deferred before the threads start.
- `bool stash(const Request&, uint32_t reporters, uint64_t forward)`: combines exactly as `publish` does into the pending buffer, then release-stores `pending`. Returns false if `written + 1 != chain` or a delta is already pending.
- `bool claim(int64_t row, uint64_t* chain)`: CAS from unclaimed to claimed.
- `pending_chain(row)` and `pending_forward(row)`.
- `pending_count(row)` and `append_pending(row, expert, slot)`: the claim winner only, staying under kDeltaMaxEntries.
- `write_pending(lease, row)`: the private `write()` with the buffer and chain, then clears `pending`.
**Guards:**
- `report`, `publish`, `publish_seed` and `write` keep their behaviour and bytes (C5).
- The staging lists a deferred write emits equal what `publish` would have written.
- The stash's release pairs with the claim's acquire.
- Nothing allocates.
**Never:**
- Change Wire or kDeltaMaxEntries (R1).

tasks.title: Deferred publication in RamTier: stash, claim on row r-1, backstop, delta_publish
tasks.intent:
With the flag on, a deferrable row's delta is stashed by its last reporter, written by the thread serving row r-1's next record, and caught by a backstop otherwise (S§1.1, C3, C5, C7).
**Steps:**
- `enable_ram_prefetch`: when `config.promote`, call `dist_.set_deferred`, marking row r iff r > 0 and some source's `config.target` is r (D4).
- `release_swapped`: take `(int64_t row, uint64_t chain)`.
- `reserve_victims_locked`: for a deferred row, the last reporter calls `stash` (with its group's forward id) instead of `publish` and does not call `release_swapped`. A false return goes to `fail_record`.
- New private `publish_pending(Group&, const Request& by, int64_t row, int trigger) -> int`:
  1. claim;
  2. call `promote_landed(Group&, int64_t row, uint64_t chain) -> int` (a stub returning 0 here, which T8 fills);
  3. `write_pending`;
  4. `release_swapped(row, chain)`;
  5. emit the InstrBuild `delta_publish` event.
- `pump_demand`: per group, track a forward id that bumps when a record's row is not greater than the previous record's row. Then, for every record that is not torn (both the served and the lapped-hot `skip` paths), before `handle_record`:
  - backstop (trigger 2, counting `kSpecPublishBackstop`): `request.row`'s own pending delta, and any pending row p < request.row stashed in an earlier forward;
  - `publish_pending(request.row + 1)` with trigger 1.
- `handle_record`: hold `group.row_mutex[request.row]` across `serve_record`/`touch_request`.
**Guards:**
- A later row of the same forward never writes row r's delta.
- The backstop runs before `classify_lanes_locked`'s chain check.
- Flag off: nothing new runs, and the order and bytes are unchanged (C5).
- One writer per (row, chain), via the CAS (R3).
- Nothing allocates on the record path.
**Never:**
- Change device code or the layout (R1).

tasks.title: Promotion at publish: map landed pool rows into the pending delta
tasks.intent:
Fill `promote_landed` so the claimer maps each landed pool row of row r into row r's pending delta, as §1.2 says (C1, C2, C4).
**Steps:**
- For each group g, lock `pool_->mutex(g)`, then `dist_.group(g).row_mutex[row]`. Then, per entry of (row, g):
  - kPoolReading: count `kSpecPromoteReading` and leave the entry.
  - kPoolLanded, with no room for 2 more entries: count `kSpecPromoteNoRoom`.
  - kPoolLanded, with no victim in g's range (no wanted list): count `kSpecPromoteNoVictim`.
  - kPoolLanded otherwise:
    - `append_pending({old,-1})` if old >= 0, then `{expert, entry.slot}`;
    - map the slot in the tier and with `publish_mirror`;
    - mark the victim kSpec;
    - set the entry to `slot = victim`, `freed_at = chain`, kPoolSwapped|kPoolNoExpert;
    - count `kSpecPromotedEarly` and record `promoted`/`promote_evicted`/`promoted_chain` in g's GroupRow.
- In `publish_pending`, when trigger 1 finds no pending delta for row r, count `kSpecPromoteNoDelta` once per landed entry of row r.
**Guards:**
- Counts go to the claimer's own group block.
- Picking a victim for group g must not count kEvictions into g's block or touch `g.tick`. Give `take_victim_locked` a counting-group parameter, or add a helper. Stamp the promoted slot with the victim's old stamp.
- Lock order: pool mutex, then row mutex (R2).
- `release_swapped(row, chain)` empties the entry after the write.
**Never:**
- Promote reading entries.
- Change `take_pooled_locked` (D2, N4).
